Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- New-onset, work-related anxiety over ~2 months with significant functional impact (dreading work, insomnia, reduced activities), plus low mood/anhedonia and palpitations. Denies suicidality. Lives with supportive parents. Alcohol (binge on weekends) and occasional smoking may contribute to sleep disturbance and anxiety (supports DDx).
- Palpitations likely anxiety-related; plan to exclude medical contributors with basic labs per transcript.
- Differential considerations consistent with DDx and transcript:
  - Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (work-related): High likelihood given clear temporal link to new stressful job, insomnia, and functional impairment.
  - Generalized anxiety disorder (early course): Moderate likelihood; pervasive worry and physical symptoms; duration <6 months.
  - Major depressive episode with anxious distress: Moderate likelihood; low mood/anhedonia, insomnia, fatigue >2 weeks with prominent anxiety.
  - Rule-outs: Hyperthyroidism and paroxysmal arrhythmia considered low likelihood but reasonable to exclude per planned basic labs.
- Plan per consultation:
  - Self-refer to NHS talking therapy (CBT-type); link to be provided.
  - Provide online resources and written sleep-hygiene guidance.
  - Safety-net: If worsening, unable to cope with work/ADLs, or no improvement with therapy/resources, contact GP; medications may be considered if needed.
  - Arrange basic blood tests via support line and schedule GP follow-up one week after tests to review results.
